To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the perception of tourism among community actors and capacity building needs varied substantially among different community actors and sub-SESs and therefore tourism development in a MPA should consider the various perceptions and capacity building needs of these actors and sub-SEs.
tourism development in a marine national park is perceived differently among different community actors and that capacity building for tourism development should be tailored to their needs.

tourism development in a marine protected areas must be tailored to the diverse needs and perceptions of the community actors and that capacity building is essential for the successful implementation of community-based MNP policies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the capacity building of local communities in tourism development in a MPA.
the capacity building required for community-based MPA policy implementation and tourism development in small-island settings.

how tourism development in a MPA can be used as an alternative economic and social development strategy in subnational small-islands settings, and how capacity building for tourism development can be implemented in a nested SES.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the capacity building for tourism development should be tailored to meet the needs of the various sub-SEs and that the support of the government is essential for the implementation of the community-based MPA.
the success of tourism development in a MPA depends on the capacity building of the various community actors in the sub-SESs and the support from governmental agencies.

capacity building for tourism development is a key issue to address in the context of a nested SES, and the capacity-building needs should be tailored to meet the needs of the various sub-SE systems in a regional placebased management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

tourism development in a MPA must consider the diverse perceptions of the local communities and that capacity building for local communities must be tailored to the different needs of the various community actors.

the success of community participation in place-based management, especially in MPA, depends on the support from governmental agencies, and the support from governmental agency depends on the capacity of the community to participate in the management.

capacity building for tourism development should be based on the social–ecological context of a nested system, and it must be tailored to the specific needs of the various subsystems and the various community actors within each subsystem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the capacity building for tourism development should not be considered in a general way.
capacity building is essential in the early stages of place-based management, and the needs of local communities and community actors must be considered when developing capacity building programs.
the community actors in different sub-SES should be considered in the capacity building and planning of tourism development.
